name: Ability Check
preview: A D20 Test using an ability, sometimes with an associated skill, to overcome a challenge.

text.body: Roll a d20, add the relevant ability modifier, and add your Proficiency Bonus if an applicable proficiency allows it.

name: Ability Score and Modifier
preview: Each of the six abilities has a score and a modifier used by many rules.

text.body: Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma each have a score and a corresponding modifier. Add the modifier whenever a rule tells you to use that ability.

name: Action
preview: On your turn, you normally have one action.

text.body: On your turn, you can take one action, choosing a standard action or another action granted by a feature or rule.

name: Advantage
preview: Roll two d20s and use the higher result.

text.body: Advantage causes you to roll two d20s for a D20 Test and use the higher roll. Multiple sources of Advantage do not stack. Advantage and Disadvantage on the same roll cancel each other.

name: Adventure
preview: An adventure is a series of encounters that produces a story through play.

text.body: Adventure is the rules term for a connected series of encounters.

name: Alignment
preview: Alignment broadly describes ethical attitudes and ideals.

text.body: Alignment combines a morality axis (Good, Evil, Neutral) with an order axis (Lawful, Chaotic, Neutral) to create the familiar nine alignments.

name: Ally
preview: An ally is a creature on your side or designated as your ally.

text.body: Party members, friends, creatures fighting on your side, and creatures designated as allies by a rule or the DM count as allies.

name: Ammunition
preview: A weapon with Ammunition needs the specified ammunition for ranged attacks.

text.body: Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing ammunition is part of the attack; loading a one-handed weapon requires a free hand. After a fight, 1 minute of searching recovers half the ammunition used, rounded down.

name: Area of Effect
preview: Many spells and effects fill a shaped area rather than targeting only one creature.

text.body: Common areas are Cone, Cube, Cylinder, Emanation, Line, and Sphere. Total Cover can block straight lines from an area's point of origin and exclude locations behind it.

name: Armor Class
preview: The target number an attack roll must meet or exceed to hit.

text.heading: Base AC
text.body: A creature's basic AC is 10 + Dexterity modifier unless armor or another rule gives a different base calculation.

text.heading: One Base Calculation
text.body: If more than one rule gives you a base AC calculation, choose which one to use; you do not combine base calculations.

name: Armor Stealth Disadvantage
preview: Some armor imposes Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

text.body: If an armor entry lists Disadvantage for Stealth, you have Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks while wearing it.

name: Armor Strength Requirement
preview: Some armor reduces Speed if your Strength is below its listed requirement.

text.body: If armor lists a Strength score and your Strength is lower, your Speed is reduced by 10 feet while wearing it.

name: Armor Training
preview: Wearing armor without training has serious drawbacks.

text.body: If you wear Light, Medium, or Heavy armor without training, you have Disadvantage on D20 Tests involving Strength or Dexterity and cannot cast spells. A Shield gives no AC bonus if you lack Shield training.

name: Attack
preview: Use the Attack action to make an attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike.

text.heading: Attack
text.body: The Attack action lets you make one attack roll with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike, unless a feature gives you more attacks.

text.heading: Equip or Unequip
text.body: When you make an attack as part of the action, you can equip or unequip one weapon before or after that attack.

text.heading: Move Between Attacks
text.body: If you can make multiple attacks, you can use movement between them.

name: Attack Roll
preview: A D20 Test used to determine whether an attack hits.

text.body: An attack roll is a D20 Test made for a weapon attack, Unarmed Strike, spell attack, or another effect that calls for one. Compare the total to the target's Armor Class.

name: Attitude
preview: A monster's attitude toward you is Friendly, Hostile, or Indifferent.

text.body: Attitude summarizes a monster's starting disposition toward a player character and can affect Influence checks.

name: Attunement
preview: Some magic items require Attunement before their magical properties can be used.

text.body: A creature can normally be attuned to no more than three magic items at one time. Individual items can set prerequisites or special rules.

name: Blinded
preview: You cannot see; sight-based checks fail and attacks are affected.

text.heading: Can't See
text.body: You cannot see and automatically fail ability checks that require sight.

text.heading: Attacks
text.body: Attack rolls against you have Advantage, and your attack rolls have Disadvantage.

name: Blindsight
preview: Blindsight lets you see within a stated range without relying on normal sight.

text.body: Within its range, Blindsight can perceive anything not behind Total Cover even if you are Blinded or in Darkness, and it can perceive Invisible creatures and objects.

name: Bloodied
preview: A creature is Bloodied while it has half its Hit Points or fewer remaining.

text.body: Bloodied is a descriptive rules state that applies when a creature has no more than half of its Hit Point maximum remaining.

name: Bonus Action
preview: A special additional action available only when a rule gives you one.

text.body: You can take no more than one Bonus Action on a turn, and you have a Bonus Action only when a rule, feature, spell, or item gives you something to do with it.

name: Breaking Objects
preview: Objects can be attacked and damaged; the DM can let fragile objects break automatically.

text.body: Objects can have Armor Class and Hit Points. A sufficiently fragile object may be broken automatically with the Attack or Utilize action at the DM's discretion.

name: Bright Light
preview: Bright Light is normal illumination.

text.body: Bright Light is ordinary illumination and does not impose the visibility penalties associated with Dim Light or Darkness.

name: Burning
preview: A burning creature or object takes Fire damage each turn until the flames are extinguished.

text.body: A burning creature or object takes 1d4 Fire damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature can use an action to fall Prone and roll to extinguish itself; dousing, submerging, or suffocating the fire also ends it.

name: Burrow Speed
preview: A Burrow Speed lets a creature move through certain loose materials.

text.body: A Burrow Speed can normally move through sand, earth, mud, or ice, but not solid rock unless another rule specifically permits it.

name: Campaign
preview: A campaign is a series of adventures.

text.body: Campaign is the rules term for an ongoing sequence of adventures.

name: Cantrip
preview: A cantrip is a level 0 spell cast without a spell slot.

text.body: Cantrips are level 0 spells and do not require spell slots unless another rule specifically says otherwise.

name: Carrying Capacity
preview: How much you can carry, drag, lift, or push depends on Strength and size.

text.heading: Small or Medium
text.body: Carry up to Strength × 15 lb.; drag, lift, or push up to Strength × 30 lb.

text.heading: Size Scaling
text.body: Tiny uses half those multipliers; Large doubles them; Huge quadruples them; Gargantuan multiplies them by eight.

text.heading: Over Carry Capacity
text.body: While dragging, lifting, or pushing more than your carrying maximum, your Speed can be no more than 5 feet.

name: Challenge Rating
preview: Challenge Rating summarizes how threatening a monster is to a typical party.

text.body: CR is a rough measure of a monster's threat to a group of four player characters; circumstances and party size can make a creature more or less dangerous than the number suggests.

name: Character Sheet
preview: The paper or digital record used to track a character's game information.

text.body: A character sheet is the paper or digital record used to track a character's abilities, features, equipment, Hit Points, and other game information.

name: Charmed
preview: You cannot harm the charmer, and the charmer has an edge socially.

text.heading: Can't Harm the Charmer
text.body: You cannot attack the charmer or target the charmer with damaging abilities or magical effects.

text.heading: Social Advantage
text.body: The charmer has Advantage on ability checks to interact with you socially.

name: Climb Speed
preview: A Climb Speed avoids the normal extra movement cost of climbing.

text.body: Use a Climb Speed to traverse vertical surfaces without the extra movement cost normally imposed by climbing.

name: Climbing
preview: Climbing normally costs extra movement unless you use a Climb Speed.

text.body: Each foot climbed costs 1 extra foot, or 2 extra feet in Difficult Terrain. A slippery surface or one with few handholds may require a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check at the DM's option.

name: Combining Spell Effects
preview: Different spells can overlap; multiple copies of the same spell do not stack.

text.body: Effects from different spells can combine while their durations overlap. Multiple castings of the same spell do not combine; use the most potent effect, or the most recent if equally potent.

name: Concentration
preview: Some spells and effects require Concentration to remain active.

text.heading: One Concentration Effect
text.body: Starting another spell or effect that requires Concentration immediately ends the Concentration you were already maintaining.

text.heading: Damage
text.body: When you take damage, make a Constitution saving throw. The DC is 10 or half the damage taken, rounded down, whichever is higher, to a maximum DC of 30.

text.heading: Incapacitated or Dead
text.body: Concentration ends if you become Incapacitated or die.

text.heading: Voluntary End
text.body: You can end your Concentration at any time without using an action.

name: Condition
preview: A condition is a temporary game state with defined effects.

text.body: Conditions do not stack with themselves; you either have a condition or you do not. Exhaustion is the exception because it has cumulative levels.

name: Cone
preview: A Cone widens as it extends from its point of origin.

text.body: A Cone extends in a chosen direction. At any distance from the origin, its width equals that distance. The origin is excluded unless the creator chooses to include it.

name: Cover
preview: Cover protects a target behind an obstacle.

text.heading: Half Cover
text.body: +2 AC and +2 to Dexterity saving throws.

text.heading: Three-Quarters Cover
text.body: +5 AC and +5 to Dexterity saving throws.

text.heading: Total Cover
text.body: The target cannot be targeted directly.

name: Crawling
preview: Crawling normally costs 1 extra foot per foot moved.

text.body: Each foot crawled costs 1 extra foot, or 2 extra feet if the space is also Difficult Terrain.

name: Creature
preview: Any being in the game, including player characters, is a creature.

text.body: Creature is the general rules term for beings in the game, including player characters and monsters.

name: Creature Type
preview: Every creature has a creature type used by rules that care about categories.

text.body: The standard creature types are Aberration, Beast, Celestial, Construct, Dragon, Elemental, Fey, Fiend, Giant, Humanoid, Monstrosity, Ooze, Plant, and Undead.

name: Critical Hit
preview: A natural 20 on an attack roll is a Critical Hit.

text.body: When the d20 for an attack roll is a 20, the attack hits regardless of modifiers or AC. Roll all of the attack's damage dice twice, add them together, then add modifiers once.

name: Cube
preview: A Cube fills a cubic area extending from a point on one of its faces.

text.body: A Cube's origin can be anywhere on one face. The origin is excluded unless the creator chooses to include it.

name: Curses
preview: A curse's creating effect defines what the curse does and how it ends.

text.body: Curses can be ended by magic that specifically removes curses, such as effects modeled on Remove Curse or Greater Restoration.

name: Cylinder
preview: A Cylinder has a radius and height around an origin at the center of its top or bottom.

text.body: A Cylinder's origin is at the center of its circular top or bottom and is included in the area.

name: D20 Test
preview: The umbrella term for ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws.

text.body: Ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws are all D20 Tests. A rule that modifies D20 Tests applies to all three unless it says otherwise.

name: Damage
preview: Damage reduces Hit Points.

text.body: Damage represents harm to a creature or object and reduces its Hit Points unless another rule changes or prevents that damage.

name: Damage Roll
preview: A die roll, modified as appropriate, that determines damage dealt.

text.body: A damage roll is a die roll plus any applicable modifiers that determines how much damage an effect deals.

name: Damage Threshold
preview: Damage below a threshold is ignored; damage that reaches it applies in full.

text.body: If a creature or object has a Damage Threshold, a single attack or effect must deal at least that amount of damage to affect its Hit Points. If the threshold is met, apply the entire damage instance.

name: Damage Types
preview: Damage is classified by type; the type matters when another rule refers to it.

text.body: The standard damage types are Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, Necrotic, Piercing, Poison, Psychic, Radiant, Slashing, and Thunder. A type has no special rule by itself; Resistance, Immunity, Vulnerability, and other effects care about the type.

name: Darkness
preview: Darkness is Heavily Obscured.

text.body: An area of Darkness counts as Heavily Obscured.

name: Darkvision
preview: Darkvision improves vision in Dim Light and Darkness within a stated range.

text.body: Within its range, Darkvision treats Dim Light as Bright Light and Darkness as Dim Light. In Darkness, colors are seen only as shades of gray.

name: Dash
preview: Gain extra movement for the current turn equal to the speed you choose to use.

text.body: When you Dash, increase the movement available to you this turn by the chosen Speed after modifiers. If you have a special speed, you can choose that speed for the Dash.

name: Dead
preview: A dead creature has no Hit Points and cannot regain them until revived.

text.body: A dead creature cannot regain Hit Points unless a revival effect first returns it to life. The creature's spirit knows who is trying to revive it and can refuse.

name: Deafened
preview: You cannot hear and automatically fail checks that require hearing.

text.body: While Deafened, you cannot hear and automatically fail any ability check that requires hearing.

name: Death Saving Throw
preview: A player character at 0 Hit Points makes a Death Save at the start of each turn.

text.heading: Roll
text.body: At the start of your turn at 0 Hit Points, make a Death Saving Throw unless you are Stable.

text.heading: Success and Failure
text.body: A 10 or higher is a success; a 9 or lower is a failure. Three successes make you Stable; three failures cause death. Successes and failures reset when you regain Hit Points or become Stable.

text.heading: Natural 1 or 20
text.body: A natural 1 counts as two failures. A natural 20 causes you to regain 1 Hit Point.

text.heading: Damage at 0 HP
text.body: Taking damage at 0 HP causes a failed Death Save; a Critical Hit causes two failures. If the damage equals or exceeds your Hit Point maximum, you die outright.

name: Dehydration
preview: Too little water causes Exhaustion that cannot be removed until enough water is consumed.

text.body: If you drink less than half your daily water requirement, gain 1 Exhaustion level at day's end. Exhaustion from dehydration cannot be removed until you drink your full daily requirement.

name: Difficult Terrain
preview: Each foot moved through Difficult Terrain costs 1 extra foot.

text.body: Moving 5 feet through Difficult Terrain normally costs 10 feet of movement. Difficult Terrain does not stack with itself.

name: Difficulty Class
preview: The target number for an ability check or saving throw.

text.body: A Difficulty Class (DC) is the number an ability check or saving throw must meet or exceed to succeed, unless the rule says otherwise.

name: Dim Light
preview: Dim Light is Lightly Obscured.

text.body: An area of Dim Light counts as Lightly Obscured.

name: Disadvantage
preview: Roll two d20s and use the lower result.

text.body: Disadvantage causes you to roll two d20s for a D20 Test and use the lower roll. Multiple sources of Disadvantage do not stack. Advantage and Disadvantage on the same roll cancel each other.

name: Disengage
preview: Your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks for the rest of the turn.

text.body: After taking the Disengage action, movement you make for the rest of the current turn does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.

name: Dodge
preview: Defend yourself until the start of your next turn.

text.heading: Attacks Against You
text.body: Attack rolls against you have Disadvantage if you can see the attacker.

text.heading: Dexterity Saves
text.body: You make Dexterity saving throws with Advantage.

text.heading: Ends Early
text.body: You lose these benefits if you become Incapacitated or your Speed becomes 0.

name: Emanation
preview: An Emanation extends outward from a creature or object and normally moves with it.

text.body: An Emanation extends in all directions from its origin. It moves with that creature or object unless the effect is instantaneous or stationary. The origin is excluded unless the creator chooses to include it.

name: Encounter
preview: An encounter is a scene involving social interaction, exploration, combat, or more than one pillar.

text.body: Encounter is a scene in an adventure that belongs to at least one of the game's major play pillars.

name: Enemy
preview: An enemy is a creature opposing or actively trying to harm you.

text.body: A creature fighting against you, actively working to harm you, or designated as an enemy by a rule or the DM counts as your enemy.

name: Exhaustion
preview: Exhaustion accumulates in levels and penalizes D20 Tests and Speed.

text.heading: Levels
text.body: Each time you gain Exhaustion, gain 1 level. At level 6, you die.

text.heading: D20 Tests
text.body: Subtract 2 from every D20 Test for each Exhaustion level.

text.heading: Speed
text.body: Reduce your Speed by 5 feet for each Exhaustion level.

text.heading: Recovery
text.body: Finishing a Long Rest removes 1 Exhaustion level. The condition ends at level 0.

name: Experience Points
preview: Characters can gain XP for overcoming challenges and adventures.

text.body: The DM awards Experience Points. Crossing level thresholds increases a character's level when the campaign uses XP advancement.

name: Expertise
preview: Expertise doubles your Proficiency Bonus for a chosen skill proficiency.

text.body: When making an ability check with a skill in which you have Expertise, double your Proficiency Bonus unless another feature is already doubling it. Expertise in the same skill does not stack.

name: Falling
preview: Falling deals 1d6 Bludgeoning damage per 10 feet, up to 20d6.

text.heading: Damage
text.body: At the end of a fall, take 1d6 Bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet fallen, to a maximum of 20d6. If you take any fall damage, you land Prone.

text.heading: Falling into Liquid
text.body: You can use your Reaction to make a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check to enter head- or feet-first; on a success, halve the fall damage.

name: Finesse
preview: A Finesse weapon can use Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage rolls.

text.body: Choose Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls of a Finesse weapon, and use the same ability for both rolls.

name: Fly Speed
preview: A Fly Speed lets you travel through the air.

text.body: A creature with a Fly Speed can stay aloft until it lands, falls, or dies, subject to the rules for Flying.

name: Flying
preview: A flying creature can fall if it is disabled unless it can hover.

text.body: While flying, you fall if you become Incapacitated or Prone or if your Fly Speed becomes 0, unless you can hover.

name: Friendly
preview: A Friendly creature views you favorably.

text.body: You have Advantage on an ability check to influence a Friendly creature.

name: Frightened
preview: Fear hinders your checks and attacks and stops you from approaching its source.

text.heading: Checks and Attacks
text.body: You have Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of fear is within line of sight.

text.heading: Can't Approach
text.body: You cannot willingly move closer to the source of your fear.

name: Grappled
preview: Your Speed is 0, some attacks are hindered, and the grappler can move you.

text.heading: Speed 0
text.body: Your Speed is 0 and cannot increase.

text.heading: Attacks
text.body: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than the grappler.

text.heading: Movable
text.body: The grappler can drag or carry you. Each foot normally costs the grappler 1 extra foot unless you are Tiny or at least two sizes smaller.

name: Grappling
preview: Rules for starting, maintaining, and ending a grapple.

text.heading: Start
text.body: Characters usually grapple through the Grapple option of an Unarmed Strike; a successful grapple gives the target the Grappled condition.

text.heading: One per Grasping Part
text.body: A free hand or other specified body part used to grapple one creature cannot grapple another or target another creature unless that grapple ends.

text.heading: Escape
text.body: A Grappled creature can use its action to make Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) against the grapple's escape DC, ending the condition on a success.

text.heading: Other Endings
text.body: The grapple ends if the grappler becomes Incapacitated, the target moves beyond the grapple's range, or the grappler releases the target. Releasing requires no action.

name: Hazard
preview: A hazard is an environmental danger.

text.body: Common rules hazards include Burning, Dehydration, Falling, Malnutrition, and Suffocation.

name: Healing
preview: Healing restores lost Hit Points up to a creature's maximum.

text.body: Healing restores Hit Points but cannot raise them above the Hit Point maximum. Rules that grant Temporary Hit Points are not healing.

name: Heavily Obscured
preview: You are effectively Blinded when trying to see something in a Heavily Obscured space.

text.body: When trying to see something in a Heavily Obscured space, you have the Blinded condition for that purpose.

name: Heavy
preview: Heavy weapons impose Disadvantage if the relevant ability score is below 13.

text.body: For a Heavy Melee weapon, you have Disadvantage on attack rolls if Strength is below 13. For a Heavy Ranged weapon, you have Disadvantage if Dexterity is below 13.

name: Help
preview: Assist an ally's ability check or distract an enemy to aid an ally's attack.

text.heading: Assist a Check
text.body: Choose a skill or tool proficiency you have and an ally close enough to assist. That ally has Advantage on its next applicable check before the start of your next turn, if the DM agrees the help is possible.

text.heading: Assist an Attack
text.body: Distract an enemy within 5 feet of you. The next attack roll by one of your allies against that enemy has Advantage if made before the start of your next turn.

name: Heroic Inspiration
preview: Spend Heroic Inspiration to reroll a die immediately after rolling it.

text.body: A player character with Heroic Inspiration can expend it to reroll any die immediately after rolling and must use the new roll. If you gain Heroic Inspiration while already having it, you can pass the new Inspiration to another player character who lacks it.

name: Hide
preview: Make a Stealth check from suitable concealment to become hidden.

text.heading: Requirements
text.body: Make a DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) check while Heavily Obscured or behind Three-Quarters or Total Cover, and while outside every enemy's line of sight.

text.heading: On a Success
text.body: You have the Invisible condition while hidden. Your Stealth total becomes the DC for a creature trying to find you with Wisdom (Perception).

text.heading: You Stop Being Hidden
text.body: You stop being hidden after making a sound louder than a whisper, being found by an enemy, making an attack roll, or casting a spell with a Verbal component.

name: High Jump
preview: With a 10-foot run-up, jump vertically 3 + your Strength modifier feet.

text.heading: Running High Jump
text.body: After moving at least 10 feet on foot, jump a number of feet equal to 3 + your Strength modifier, minimum 0.

text.heading: Standing High Jump
text.body: Without the run-up, jump half that height.

text.heading: Vertical Reach
text.body: During the jump, you can extend your arms half your height above yourself, for a total reach of the jump height plus 1.5 times your height.

name: Hit Point Dice
preview: Hit Point Dice help determine Hit Points and can be spent during a Short Rest to heal.

text.heading: Short Rest
text.body: During a Short Rest, you can spend Hit Point Dice one at a time. Roll a spent die, add your Constitution modifier, and regain at least 1 Hit Point from that die.

name: Hit Points
preview: Hit Points measure how difficult a creature or object is to kill or destroy.

text.body: Damage reduces Hit Points and healing restores them. Hit Points cannot exceed the maximum or fall below 0.

name: Hostile
preview: A Hostile creature views you unfavorably.

text.body: You have Disadvantage on an ability check to influence a Hostile creature.

name: Hover
preview: Hovering can keep a flying creature aloft in situations that would normally make it fall.

text.body: A creature that can hover can remain aloft in certain circumstances that would otherwise cause a flying creature to fall, such as becoming Prone, Incapacitated, or having its Fly Speed reduced to 0.

name: Illusions
preview: An illusion's creating effect defines what senses or mental faculties it deceives.

text.body: Illusions are insubstantial and weightless unless their rule says otherwise, but they can appear to interact naturally with the environment, such as casting shadows or echoes.

name: Immunity
preview: Immunity means the specified damage type or condition does not affect you.

text.body: If you have Immunity to a damage type or condition, that damage type or condition does not affect you.

name: Improvised Weapons
preview: Objects used as makeshift weapons normally deal 1d4 damage and lack proficiency.

text.heading: Proficiency
text.body: Do not add your Proficiency Bonus to an improvised weapon attack unless the DM treats the object as an actual weapon it resembles.

text.heading: Damage
text.body: A basic improvised weapon deals 1d4 damage of a type the DM considers appropriate.

text.heading: Thrown Range
text.body: A thrown improvised weapon has normal range 20 feet and long range 60 feet.

name: Incapacitated
preview: You cannot take actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions, and your Concentration ends.

text.heading: Inactive
text.body: You cannot take an action, Bonus Action, or Reaction.

text.heading: No Concentration
text.body: Your Concentration is broken.

text.heading: Speechless
text.body: You cannot speak.

text.heading: Initiative
text.body: If you are Incapacitated when Initiative is rolled, you have Disadvantage on the roll.

name: Indifferent
preview: An Indifferent creature has no desire to help or hinder you.

text.body: Indifferent is the default attitude for a monster unless another rule or the DM establishes a different attitude.

name: Influence
preview: Try to persuade, deceive, intimidate, amuse, or coax a monster.

text.body: Describe what you want and how you communicate it. The DM decides whether the target is willing, unwilling, or hesitant. A hesitant target may call for an appropriate ability check, such as Deception, Intimidation, Performance, Persuasion, or Animal Handling.

name: Initiative
preview: Initiative determines turn order in combat.

text.body: Roll Initiative as directed by the combat rules. A creature's Initiative score is 10 + Dexterity modifier; if using that score instead of rolling, add 5 for Advantage or subtract 5 for Disadvantage.

name: Invisible
preview: You are concealed from creatures that cannot see you, and attacks are affected.

text.heading: Initiative
text.body: If you are Invisible when you roll Initiative, you have Advantage on the roll.

text.heading: Concealed
text.body: Effects that require seeing their target cannot affect you unless the creator can somehow see you. Your worn and carried equipment is concealed too.

text.heading: Attacks
text.body: Attack rolls against you have Disadvantage and your attack rolls have Advantage, unless the other creature can somehow see you.

name: Jumping
preview: A jump is either a Long Jump or a High Jump.

text.body: Use Long Jump for horizontal distance and High Jump for vertical height. Each foot jumped uses a foot of movement.

name: Knocking Out a Creature
preview: A melee attack can knock a creature out instead of reducing it to 0 HP.

text.body: When a melee attack would reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, you can instead leave it at 1 HP, give it the Unconscious condition, and start a Short Rest. It wakes if it regains Hit Points or receives successful first aid.

name: Light
preview: Attacking with a Light weapon can enable one extra attack with another Light weapon.

text.body: When you take the Attack action and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack later that turn as a Bonus Action with a different Light weapon. Do not add your ability modifier to that extra attack's damage unless the modifier is negative.

name: Lightly Obscured
preview: Seeing through a Lightly Obscured space makes visual Perception checks harder.

text.body: You have Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks made to see something in a Lightly Obscured space.

name: Line
preview: A Line extends straight from its point of origin with a specified length and width.

text.body: A Line covers a straight path with a stated length and width. Its origin is excluded unless the creator chooses to include it.

name: Loading
preview: A Loading weapon can fire only one piece of ammunition per action, Bonus Action, or Reaction used to fire it.

text.body: Regardless of how many attacks you can normally make, a Loading weapon can fire only one piece of ammunition when you use an action, Bonus Action, or Reaction to fire it.

name: Long Jump
preview: With a 10-foot run-up, jump horizontally up to your Strength score in feet.

text.heading: Running Long Jump
text.body: Move at least 10 feet immediately before the jump to leap up to your Strength score in feet.

text.heading: Standing Long Jump
text.body: Without the run-up, the maximum distance is half as far.

text.heading: Landing in Difficult Terrain
text.body: Make a DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or become Prone.

text.heading: Low Obstacles
text.body: The DM may call for a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check to clear a low obstacle no taller than one-quarter of the jump's distance.

name: Long Rest
preview: An 8-hour extended rest that restores Hit Points, Hit Point Dice, ability scores, and some features.

text.heading: Duration
text.body: A Long Rest lasts at least 8 hours, including at least 6 hours of sleep and no more than 2 hours of light activity. You must have at least 1 Hit Point to start.

text.heading: Benefits
text.body: Regain all lost Hit Points and spent Hit Point Dice, restore reduced ability scores, reduce Exhaustion by 1, and recharge features that say they return on a Long Rest.

text.heading: Frequency
text.body: After finishing a Long Rest, wait at least 16 hours before starting another.

text.heading: Interruptions
text.body: Initiative, a non-cantrip spell, damage, or 1 hour of walking or similar exertion interrupts the rest. If at least 1 hour was completed, you gain Short Rest benefits. You may resume, adding 1 hour per interruption.

name: Magic
preview: Cast a spell with a casting time of an action or use a magical feature that requires the Magic action.

text.heading: Magic Action
text.body: Use the Magic action for a spell with a casting time of an action or for a feature or magic item that specifically requires this action.

text.heading: Long Casting Times
text.body: For a spell with a casting time of 1 minute or longer, take the Magic action on each turn and maintain Concentration during the casting.

name: Magical Effect
preview: An effect is magical if it comes from a spell, magic item, or a phenomenon explicitly called magical.

text.body: An effect counts as magical when it is created by a spell, magic item, or another rule that labels the phenomenon magical.

name: Malnutrition
preview: Too little food can cause Exhaustion.

text.body: If you eat less than half your daily food requirement, make a DC 10 Constitution save at day's end or gain 1 Exhaustion level. Eating nothing for 5 days causes Exhaustion automatically and additional levels on later days without food.

name: Material Component
preview: A Material component requires the specified material or a permitted substitute.

text.heading: Hand
text.body: You need a free hand to access Material components, and that can be the same hand used for Somatic components.

text.heading: Pouch or Focus
text.body: If the material is not consumed and has no listed cost, you can use a Component Pouch or an allowed Spellcasting Focus instead.

text.heading: Costly or Consumed Materials
text.body: A focus or pouch cannot replace a Material component that has a listed cost or is consumed.

name: Melee Attacks
preview: A melee attack normally targets something within your reach.

text.body: A melee attack allows you to attack a target within your reach, usually with a melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike.

name: Monster
preview: A monster is a creature controlled by the DM.

text.body: In the rules, any creature controlled by the DM is a monster, even if it is friendly or benevolent.

name: Nonplayer Character
preview: An NPC is a named monster with a distinct personality.

text.body: A nonplayer character (NPC) is a DM-controlled monster presented as an individual with a personal name and distinct personality.

name: Object
preview: An object is a distinct nonliving thing.

text.body: Composite structures such as buildings can consist of multiple objects for rules purposes.

name: Occupied Space
preview: A space is occupied if a creature is in it or objects completely fill it.

text.body: A space counts as occupied when a creature is there or when objects completely fill the space.

name: One Spell with a Spell Slot per Turn
preview: On a turn, you can expend only one spell slot to cast a spell.

text.body: During a single turn, you can expend only one spell slot to cast a spell. This prevents, for example, spending a slot on an action spell and another slot on a Bonus Action spell during the same turn.

name: Opportunity Attacks
preview: A Reaction that can punish a creature you can see for leaving your reach.

text.heading: Trigger
text.body: A creature you can see leaves your reach using its action, Bonus Action, Reaction, or one of its speeds.

text.heading: Attack
text.body: Use your Reaction to make one melee attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike against the creature.

text.heading: Timing
text.body: The attack occurs immediately before the creature leaves your reach.

name: Paralyzed
preview: You are Incapacitated, your Speed is 0, and nearby hits become Critical Hits.

text.heading: Incapacitated
text.body: You also have the Incapacitated condition.

text.heading: Speed and Saves
text.body: Your Speed is 0 and cannot increase. You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

text.heading: Attacks
text.body: Attack rolls against you have Advantage. Any attack roll that hits you from within 5 feet is a Critical Hit.

name: Passive Perception
preview: A score used when noticing something without actively making a Perception check.

text.body: Passive Perception equals 10 + your Wisdom (Perception) check bonus. Add 5 if you have Advantage on such checks or subtract 5 if you have Disadvantage.

name: Per Day
preview: A limited use described as 'per day' refreshes after a Long Rest.

text.body: If a rule says something can be used a certain number of times per day, finishing a Long Rest restores those uses after you run out.

name: Petrified
preview: You become an inanimate substance and suffer severe restrictions.

text.heading: Transformation
text.body: You and nonmagical gear you wear or carry become a solid inanimate substance; your weight increases tenfold and you stop aging.

text.heading: Disabled
text.body: You are Incapacitated, your Speed is 0, and you automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saves.

text.heading: Defenses
text.body: Attack rolls against you have Advantage, you have Resistance to all damage, and you are immune to the Poisoned condition.

name: Player Character
preview: A player character is a character controlled by a player.

text.body: Player character (PC) is the rules term for a character controlled by a player rather than the DM.

name: Poisoned
preview: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

text.body: While Poisoned, you have Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

name: Possession
preview: A possessing effect defines how possession works.

text.body: The rule that causes possession controls its details. Some protective or cleansing magic can prevent or end possession when specifically stated.

name: Proficiency
preview: Proficiency lets you add your Proficiency Bonus to an applicable D20 Test.

text.body: If you are proficient with the skill, save, weapon, or tool being used for a D20 Test, add your Proficiency Bonus when the rule permits it.

name: Prone
preview: Your movement is restricted and attack rolls are affected by distance.

text.heading: Movement
text.body: You can crawl or spend movement equal to half your Speed, rounded down, to stand. If your Speed is 0, you cannot stand this way.

text.heading: Your Attacks
text.body: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls.

text.heading: Attacks Against You
text.body: An attack against you has Advantage if the attacker is within 5 feet; otherwise it has Disadvantage.

name: Ranged Attacks
preview: Ranged attacks can target only creatures or objects within the attack's permitted range.

text.heading: Single Range
text.body: If an attack has one range value, you cannot attack a target beyond that distance.

text.heading: Normal and Long Range
text.body: If an attack lists two range values, the smaller is normal range and the larger is long range. Attacks beyond normal range have Disadvantage; targets beyond long range cannot be attacked.

name: Ranged Attacks in Close Combat
preview: Ranged attack rolls are harder when an enemy is right next to you.

text.body: You have Disadvantage on a ranged attack roll if you are within 5 feet of an enemy who can see you and does not have the Incapacitated condition.

name: Reach
preview: A creature's default reach is 5 feet unless a rule says otherwise.

text.body: Unless a feature, size rule, weapon, or effect says otherwise, a creature's reach is 5 feet.

name: Reaction
preview: A special action taken in response to a defined trigger.

text.body: You can take a Reaction on another creature's turn or your own turn when its trigger occurs. After taking one, you can't take another until the start of your next turn.

name: Ready
preview: Set a trigger and prepare an action or movement to use with your Reaction.

text.heading: Choose a Trigger
text.body: Describe a perceivable circumstance and choose an action or movement up to your Speed to use if it occurs before the start of your next turn.

text.heading: Reaction
text.body: When the trigger finishes, you may use your Reaction to do the readied response or ignore the trigger.

text.heading: Ready a Spell
text.body: The spell must have a casting time of an action. You cast it when you Ready it, expend any resources then, and maintain Concentration until you release it with your Reaction or the opportunity expires.

name: Resistance
preview: Resistance halves damage of the specified type.

text.body: If you have Resistance to a damage type, halve that damage against you and round down. Resistance applies only once to a single instance of damage.

name: Restrained
preview: Your Speed is 0, attacks are affected, and Dexterity saves are harder.

text.heading: Speed 0
text.body: Your Speed is 0 and cannot increase.

text.heading: Attacks
text.body: Attack rolls against you have Advantage, and your attack rolls have Disadvantage.

text.heading: Dexterity Saves
text.body: You have Disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.

name: Ritual
preview: A prepared spell with the Ritual tag can be cast without a spell slot by taking 10 extra minutes.

text.body: If you have a Ritual spell prepared, you can cast it as a Ritual. It takes 10 minutes longer, expends no spell slot, and therefore cannot be cast at a higher level by using a slot.

name: Round Down
preview: Fractions are normally rounded down.

text.body: Whenever a game rule has you multiply or divide and the result is a fraction, round down unless that rule specifically tells you to round up.

name: Saving Throw
preview: A D20 Test made to avoid or resist a threat.

text.heading: When You Roll
text.body: You normally make a saving throw only when a rule requires one. The effect tells you which ability to use and what success or failure means.

text.heading: Choosing to Fail
text.body: You can choose to fail a saving throw without rolling unless another rule says otherwise.

text.heading: Missing Ability Score
text.body: If a target is forced to make a save and lacks the required ability score, it automatically fails.

name: Search
preview: Make a Wisdom check to notice something that isn't obvious.

text.body: The Search action normally uses a Wisdom check. Common examples are Insight for a creature's state of mind, Medicine for an ailment or cause of death, Perception for concealed creatures or objects, and Survival for tracks or food.

name: Shape-Shifting
preview: A shape-shifting effect tells you what changes; ongoing effects normally carry over.

text.body: Unless the effect says otherwise, conditions, spells, curses, and other ongoing effects remain on you across forms. You revert to your true form if you die.

name: Short Rest
preview: A 1-hour downtime period that can restore Hit Points through Hit Point Dice and recharge some features.

text.heading: Requirements
text.body: A Short Rest lasts 1 hour and begins only if you have at least 1 Hit Point. During it, do nothing more strenuous than reading, talking, eating, or standing watch.

text.heading: Hit Point Dice
text.body: At the end, spend any number of Hit Point Dice one at a time. Roll each die, add Constitution modifier, and regain at least 1 Hit Point from each die spent.

text.heading: Interrupted
text.body: Rolling Initiative, casting a spell other than a cantrip, or taking damage interrupts the rest and grants no benefits.

name: Simultaneous Effects
preview: The creature or DM whose turn it is decides the order of simultaneous effects.

text.body: If two or more things happen at the same time on a turn, the player or DM controlling that turn decides the order in which those effects are resolved.

name: Size
aliases: tiny small medium large huge gargantuan
preview: Creatures and objects use size categories from Tiny through Gargantuan.

text.body: The size categories are Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, and Gargantuan. Creature size affects occupied space and several other rules; object size can affect Hit Points.

name: Skill
preview: A specialization associated with an ability check.

text.body: A skill represents an area of specialization. If you have proficiency in the skill used for an ability check, you can add your Proficiency Bonus.

name: Somatic Component
preview: A Somatic component requires at least one hand to perform the spell's gestures.

text.body: A spellcaster must use at least one hand to perform a spell's Somatic component.

name: Speed
preview: Speed is the distance in feet a creature can cover when it moves on its turn.

text.heading: Using Multiple Speeds
text.body: If you have more than one speed, you can switch during a move. Subtract the distance already moved from the new speed to determine how much farther you can move.

text.heading: Changes Apply to Special Speeds
text.body: A temporary increase or decrease to your Speed also changes your special speeds by the same amount unless a rule says otherwise.

name: Spell
preview: A spell is a magical effect defined by its spell description.

text.body: Spell descriptions specify level, school, casting time, range, components, duration, and effects. The general spellcasting rules explain how those entries work.

name: Spell Attack
preview: A spell attack is an attack roll made as part of a spell or magical effect.

text.body: Resolve a spell attack as an attack roll, using the spell attack modifier provided by the relevant spellcasting rule.

name: Spell Attack Modifier
preview: Your spell attack modifier is spellcasting ability modifier + Proficiency Bonus.

text.body: For a spell attack roll, add your spellcasting ability modifier and Proficiency Bonus unless a rule gives another formula.

name: Spell Casting Time
preview: A spell's Casting Time tells you what action or amount of time is required to cast it.

text.heading: Common Casting Times
text.body: Most spells use the Magic action, but some use a Bonus Action, Reaction, or take 1 minute or longer.

text.heading: Long Casting Times
text.body: For a casting time of 1 minute or longer, take the Magic action on each turn and maintain Concentration. If Concentration breaks, the spell fails without expending the spell slot.

name: Spell Components
preview: A spell can require Verbal, Somatic, and Material components.

text.body: If you cannot provide every component a spell requires, you cannot cast it.

name: Spell Duration
preview: A spell's Duration tells you how long its magic persists.

text.heading: Concentration
text.body: A Concentration duration follows the Concentration rules.

text.heading: Instantaneous
text.body: The magic exists only for a moment.

text.heading: Time Span
text.body: A timed spell lasts for the listed period. While a timed spell you cast continues, you can dismiss it with no action unless you are Incapacitated.

name: Spell Range
preview: A spell's range limits where its effect can originate.

text.heading: Distance
text.body: A distance range is given in feet.

text.heading: Touch
text.body: The spell's effect originates on something the caster must touch within their reach.

text.heading: Self
text.body: The spell is cast on the caster or emanates from the caster.

text.heading: Movable Effects
text.body: After creation, a movable spell effect is not limited by the spell's original range unless the spell says otherwise.

name: Spell Save DC
preview: Your spell save DC is 8 + spellcasting ability modifier + Proficiency Bonus.

text.body: When one of your spells calls for a saving throw, its standard save DC is 8 + your spellcasting ability modifier + your Proficiency Bonus unless a rule says otherwise.

name: Spell Slots
preview: Spell slots are expended to cast most level 1+ spells.

text.heading: Using a Slot
text.body: To cast a level 1+ spell with a spell slot, expend a slot of the spell's level or higher.

text.heading: Higher-Level Slot
text.body: A spell cast using a higher-level slot counts as that higher level for that casting; some spells gain stronger effects as described in the spell.

text.heading: Recovery
text.body: The standard spellcasting rules restore expended spell slots after a Long Rest, though class features can create exceptions.

name: Spell Targets
preview: A spell's description identifies what it can target.

text.heading: Clear Path
text.body: To target something with a spell, you need a clear path to it; a target behind Total Cover cannot normally be targeted.

text.heading: Target Yourself
text.body: If a spell targets a creature of your choice, you can usually choose yourself unless it requires a Hostile creature or specifically another creature.

text.heading: Invalid Target
text.body: If the chosen target cannot be affected, the spell has no effect on that target; a spell slot used to cast the spell is still expended.

name: Spellcasting Focus
preview: An allowed focus can replace certain Material components.

text.body: A Spellcasting Focus can replace a spell's Material component when the material is not consumed and has no specified cost, if your spellcasting feature allows that kind of focus.

name: Sphere
preview: A Sphere extends outward from its point of origin by a stated radius.

text.body: A Sphere extends equally in all directions from its origin, and the origin is included.

name: Stable
preview: A Stable creature has 0 Hit Points but is not making Death Saving Throws.

text.body: A creature is Stable when it has 0 Hit Points but is no longer required to make Death Saving Throws. It remains at 0 HP until healed or another rule changes its state.

name: Stat Block
preview: A stat block presents the game statistics of a monster.

text.body: A monster stat block summarizes size, creature type, alignment, AC, Initiative, Hit Points, Speed, ability scores, saves, skills, defenses, senses, languages, Challenge Rating, traits, actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, and attack/save notation as applicable.

name: Study
preview: Make an Intelligence check to recall or uncover information.

text.body: The Study action uses an Intelligence check to examine memory, books, clues, or other knowledge sources. Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, and Religion are common applicable skills.

name: Stunned
preview: You are Incapacitated, fail Strength and Dexterity saves, and attacks against you have Advantage.

text.heading: Incapacitated
text.body: You have the Incapacitated condition.

text.heading: Saves
text.body: You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

text.heading: Attacks
text.body: Attack rolls against you have Advantage.

name: Suffocation
preview: After you run out of breath, you gain Exhaustion each turn until you can breathe again.

text.body: You can hold your breath for 1 + Constitution modifier minutes, with a minimum of 30 seconds. Once you run out of breath or begin choking, gain 1 Exhaustion level at the end of each turn. When you can breathe again, remove all Exhaustion gained from suffocating.

name: Surprise
preview: A creature caught unaware at the start of combat has Disadvantage on Initiative.

text.body: If a creature is surprised when combat begins, it has Disadvantage on its Initiative roll.

name: Swim Speed
preview: A Swim Speed avoids the normal extra movement cost of swimming.

text.body: Use a Swim Speed to swim without the extra movement normally required.

name: Swimming
preview: Swimming normally costs extra movement unless you use a Swim Speed.

text.body: Each foot swum costs 1 extra foot, or 2 extra feet in Difficult Terrain. Rough water may require a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check at the DM's option.

name: Target
preview: A target is the creature or object selected by an attack, save-based effect, spell, or other rule.

text.body: A target is a creature or object selected by an attack roll, forced to make a saving throw by an effect, or chosen to receive a spell or other phenomenon.

name: Telepathy
preview: Telepathy allows mental communication within a specified range.

text.body: Unless a rule says otherwise, the target need not share a language but must understand at least one language or be telepathic. Incapacitation, leaving range, or contacting a different creature breaks the connection.

name: Teleportation
preview: Teleportation moves you instantly without crossing the intervening space.

text.heading: No Movement Cost
text.body: Teleportation does not expend movement unless its rule says otherwise and never provokes Opportunity Attacks.

text.heading: Gear
text.body: Equipment you wear and carry teleports with you. Another creature does not come with you unless the effect says it does.

text.heading: Blocked Destination
text.body: If the destination is occupied or blocked by a solid obstacle, appear in the nearest unoccupied space of your choice.

name: Temporary Hit Points
preview: Temporary Hit Points absorb damage before your normal Hit Points.

text.heading: Buffer
text.body: When you have Temporary Hit Points and take damage, subtract the damage from the temporary pool first; excess damage carries over to normal Hit Points.

text.heading: No Stacking
text.body: Temporary Hit Points from different sources do not add together unless a rule says otherwise; when you gain a new amount, choose whether to keep the old amount or take the new one.

text.heading: Not Healing
text.body: Temporary Hit Points are not normal Hit Points and do not count as healing.

name: Thrown
preview: A Thrown weapon can be thrown to make a ranged attack.

text.body: You can draw a Thrown weapon as part of the attack. If it is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the ranged attack and damage that you would use for a melee attack with it.

name: Tremorsense
preview: Tremorsense pinpoints creatures and moving objects sharing the same surface or liquid.

text.body: Within its range, Tremorsense can pinpoint creatures and moving objects in contact with the same surface or liquid as you. It cannot detect things in the air and is not a form of sight.

name: Truesight
preview: Truesight pierces several kinds of visual deception within its range.

text.body: Within its range, Truesight sees through normal and magical Darkness, sees Invisible creatures and objects, recognizes visual illusions, discerns true forms of transformed creatures or objects, and sees into the Ethereal Plane.

name: Two-Handed
preview: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

text.body: You need two hands to make an attack with a Two-Handed weapon.

name: Unarmed Strike
preview: Use your body in melee to deal damage, grapple, or shove.

text.heading: Damage
text.body: Make an attack roll using Strength + Proficiency Bonus. On a hit, deal Bludgeoning damage equal to 1 + your Strength modifier.

text.heading: Grapple
text.body: The target makes a Strength or Dexterity save against DC 8 + your Strength modifier + Proficiency Bonus. On a failure it becomes Grappled. The target can be no more than one size larger, and you need a free hand.

text.heading: Shove
text.body: The target makes a Strength or Dexterity save against DC 8 + your Strength modifier + Proficiency Bonus. On a failure, push it 5 feet away or give it the Prone condition. The target can be no more than one size larger.

name: Unconscious
preview: You are Incapacitated and Prone, drop what you hold, and nearby hits become Critical Hits.

text.heading: Inert
text.body: You have the Incapacitated and Prone conditions and drop whatever you are holding. When Unconscious ends, you remain Prone.

text.heading: Speed and Saves
text.body: Your Speed is 0 and cannot increase. You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

text.heading: Attacks
text.body: Attack rolls against you have Advantage. Any attack that hits from within 5 feet is a Critical Hit.

text.heading: Unaware
text.body: You are unaware of your surroundings.

name: Unoccupied Space
preview: A space is unoccupied if it contains no creature and is not completely filled by objects.

text.body: A space counts as unoccupied when no creature is there and objects do not completely fill it.

name: Utilize
preview: Use an object when its use requires an action.

text.body: You can often interact with an object as part of another activity, but when an object's rules require an action to use it, take the Utilize action.

name: Verbal Component
preview: A Verbal component must be spoken in a normal speaking voice.

text.body: A spell with a Verbal component requires the caster to utter the component in a normal speaking voice. A gagged creature or a creature in magical silence cannot provide it.

name: Versatile
preview: A Versatile weapon can be used one- or two-handed, with a larger damage die in two hands.

text.body: A Versatile weapon lists a parenthetical damage value. Use that value when making a melee attack with the weapon in two hands.

name: Vulnerability
preview: Vulnerability doubles damage of the specified type.

text.body: If you have Vulnerability to a damage type, double that damage against you. Vulnerability applies only once to a single instance of damage.

name: Weapon
preview: Weapons are Simple or Martial and are also classified as Melee or Ranged.

text.body: A weapon's entry lists category, whether it is Melee or Ranged, damage, properties, mastery, weight, and cost.

name: Weapon Attack
preview: A weapon attack is an attack roll made with a weapon.

text.body: Resolve a weapon attack as an attack roll and apply proficiency and the weapon's relevant ability modifier as directed by the weapon rules.

name: Weapon Proficiency
preview: Proficiency with a weapon lets you add your Proficiency Bonus to attack rolls made with it.

text.body: Anyone can wield a weapon, but you add your Proficiency Bonus to an attack roll with it only if you are proficient with that weapon.

name: Weapon Property: Reach
preview: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach for attacks and Opportunity Attacks with it.

text.body: When attacking with a Reach weapon, add 5 feet to your reach. Use that increased reach when determining Opportunity Attacks with that weapon.

name: Weapon Range
preview: Two numbers such as 80/320 mean normal range / long range in feet.

text.heading: First Number
text.body: The first number is normal range. Attacks at or within it are made normally unless another rule applies.

text.heading: Second Number
text.body: The second number is long range. Attacks beyond normal range but at or within long range have Disadvantage.

text.heading: Beyond Long Range
text.body: You cannot attack a target beyond the weapon's long range.
